is.je: Unstressed third-person singular of biti: he/she/it is. Also a past-tense auxiliary and a short form of 'her'.

that; yes.da: Means 'yes' as an answer, or introduces a clause ('that'). Other uses depend on the construction.

oneself.se: Short reflexive pronoun, used with verbs such as prati se. It has no single English equivalent and does not mean 'are'.
oneself.sebe: Stressed genitive/accusative reflexive pronoun. It can refer to any grammatical person, not only 'yourself'.
oneself.sobom: Instrumental reflexive pronoun; often with s/sa ('with oneself'). It can refer to any person.

and.i: The basic word for 'and' that connects similar things.
and.a: A contrastive conjunction, often translated as 'and' or 'but', used to show a slight contrast.
and.pa: A conjunction used to show consequence or continuation, like 'and then' or 'so'.

in.u: With locative for location ('in'); with accusative for movement into somewhere. Also means 'at' in time expressions.
in.unutra: An adverb meaning 'inside', typically used to describe location or motion.

that; it.to: Neuter singular demonstrative, nominative/accusative. Can stand for 'that' or 'it'.

I am; alone.sam: Usually the short first-person singular of biti, also a past-tense auxiliary. As an adjective, sam means 'alone' (masculine).

what.što: The standard word for 'what' in questions and statements.
what.kakav: Means 'what kind of' or 'what type', used for descriptions.

on.na: Indicates location or direction, meaning 'on' in a physical sense.

you.ti: Informal singular subject 'you'; also the short dative pronoun 'to you'. Context distinguishes them.
you.vas: Genitive/accusative of plural or polite vi. The possessive 'your' is vaš, not vas.
you.vi: The formal or plural subject pronoun for 'you'.
you.tebe: Long, stressed genitive/accusative of ti. Used after prepositions or for emphasis; short form te.
you.vama: Dative/locative/instrumental plural or polite singular: to/about/with you. Short dative: vam.

we; to me.mi: Either the subject pronoun 'we' or the short dative 'to me'. These are different pronouns with the same spelling.

you are.ste: The formal or plural form of 'you are'.
you are.jesi: The emphatic or interrogative form of 'si' (you are).
you are.jeste: Stressed second-person plural of biti, also used for polite singular address. Standard Croatian third-person singular is jest.

(question particle).li: Unstressed particle used in yes/no questions, usually after a verb: znaš li? It has no direct English translation.

I.ja: First-person singular subject pronoun. Often omitted because the verb already identifies the person.

are.su: Short third-person plural of biti: 'they are'; also used as a past-tense auxiliary.

but.ali: The standard word for 'but', used for contrast.
but.no: A slightly more formal or softer alternative to 'ali', often used at the start of a sentence.

is not.nije: Negative third-person singular of biti. With a past participle, forms a negative past tense.

with; from.s: With instrumental means 'with'; with genitive can mean 'from/off'. Sa is a longer pronunciation variant.
with; from.sa: Longer form of s, especially before s, z, š, ž and in sa mnom. Case determines 'with' versus 'from/off'.

only.samo: The most common word for 'only', meaning 'just' or 'merely'.
only.tek: Means 'only' in the sense of 'not until' or 'just now'.

him; it.ga: Short genitive/accusative pronoun for masculine or neuter singular: 'him/it', with the English wording set by context.
him; it.njim: Instrumental masculine/neuter singular pronoun. Used after prepositions, such as s njim ('with him/it').

me.me: Short genitive/accusative of ja. The longer, stressed form is mene.
me.mene: Long, stressed genitive/accusative of ja. Used after prepositions, for contrast or emphasis; short form me.

would.bi: Conditional auxiliary for ti, on/ona/ono and oni/one/ona; used with a past participle. First-person singular uses bih.

this.ovo: The neuter form of 'this', used for objects close by.
this.ovaj: The masculine form of 'this', used for masculine nouns.
this.ta: Feminine demonstrative that can mean 'that' or 'this' depending on context.
this.ova: The feminine form of 'this', used for feminine nouns.
this.ovim: Instrumental form of 'ovaj', meaning 'by this' or 'with this'.

how.kako: The standard word for 'how' in questions and statements.

you; and.te: Short genitive/accusative of ti ('you'); also a conjunction meaning 'and'.

will.će: Short future auxiliary for third-person singular or plural: he/she/it/they will. Used with an infinitive.
will.hoće: Full verb form of 'will/wants' that can be used alone or in questions.
will.volje: Genitive or plural form of 'volja', which means 'will' as in personal willpower.
will.volja: Nominative singular; genitive plural of volja (feminine noun).

about; on.o: With locative usually means 'about'; accusative occurs in expressions of contact or time, such as o zid and o Božić.

good.dobro: The neuter form of 'good', also used as an adverb meaning 'well'.
good.dobrim: Dative/instrumental plural of 'dobar', meaning 'to good' or 'with good'.
good.dobroj: Dative/locative feminine of 'dobar', meaning 'to good' or 'in good'.

if.ako: The standard word for 'if' in conditional sentences.
if.ukoliko: A more formal or conditional version of 'ako', often used in writing or polite speech.

we are.smo: The standard first-person plural of the verb 'to be'.
we are.jesmo: Emphatic version of 'smo', used to affirm or contrast.

all.sve: Often 'everything' (neuter singular); also several plural/case forms of sav. The noun and construction determine agreement.
all.svi: The masculine plural form of 'all', often meaning 'everyone'.
all.sva: Feminine or neuter plural for 'all things'.
all.svu: Accusative feminine singular of 'sav', meaning 'all' or 'entire'.

I will.ću: First-person singular future auxiliary. It can precede the infinitive or follow its shortened form: ću raditi / radit ću.
I will.hoću: Full form meaning both 'I want' and 'I will'.

be.biti: The infinitive form of the verb 'to be'.
be.bude: Third-person singular perfective present of biti; also used in subordinate clauses and wishes.

I know.znam: The most common form, meaning 'I know' a fact or skill.
I know.poznajem: Used when you are familiar with someone/something personally.
I know.poznam: First-person singular present of poznati (know/be acquainted with). Poznajem is from poznavati.

I am not.nisam: Negative first-person singular of biti. With a past participle it gives 'I did not/have not'; alone it means 'I am not'.

here.tu: Usually 'here/there at that place'; can also be a feminine accusative form of taj ('that').
here.evo: Used to introduce or present something, like 'here it is!'.
here.ovamo: Means 'over here' or 'this way', indicating movement toward the speaker.

was.bio: Masculine singular past participle of biti. Usually combines with an auxiliary: bio sam ('I was').
was.bila: Past participle of biti: feminine singular or neuter plural. An auxiliary identifies the person.

I can; they can.mogu: Present of moći, first-person singular or third-person plural. Both forms have the same spelling.

why.zašto: The standard and most common word for 'why' in questions.
why.čemu: Literally means 'to what purpose' or 'for what', used in more formal or rhetorical questions.

more.još: Means 'more' in the sense of 'still' or 'additional'.
more.više: Comparative form meaning 'more' in quantity or degree.

order.redu: Dative/locative singular of red. The phrase u redu means 'all right' or 'OK'.

was; any; either.bilo: Neuter singular past participle of biti. Also appears in bilo tko ('anyone') and bilo…bilo ('either…or').

something.nešto: The standard and most common word for 'something'.
something.štogod: Indefinite pronoun meaning something. Written separately, što god means whatever.
something.nečeg: Short genitive form of nešto (something); nečega is the longer standard form.
something.nečem: Short dative/locative form of nešto (something); nečemu is the longer standard form.

when.kad: Short form of kada ('when'); standard Croatian, not restricted to informal speech.
when.kada: Means 'when'; kad is a standard shorter variant. Both are used in questions and time clauses.

which; who.koji: Masculine singular interrogative/relative form. Unlike tko, it agrees with the noun it refers to.

I think.mislim: The most common verb for 'I think', in the sense of 'I believe' or 'I suppose'.
I think.smatram: More formal, meaning 'I consider' or 'I deem'.
I think.razmislim: Perfective form meaning 'I think it over' or 'I reflect'.
I think.pomislim: Used for a sudden or brief thought.

thanks.hvala: The standard and universally used word for 'thanks' or 'thank you'.

from.iz: A preposition meaning 'from' a place or source.

perhaps.možda: Adverb meaning maybe/perhaps. It expresses uncertainty, not a grammatical future tense.

them.ih: Short genitive/accusative plural pronoun ('them'); the stressed form is njih.
them.njih: Full genitive/accusative plural pronoun (them), used after prepositions or for emphasis. Short form: ih.
them.njima: Dative/locative/instrumental plural pronoun: to/about/with them. Short dative: im.

where.gdje: Standard word for 'where' in questions about location.
where.kuda: Used similarly to 'kamo' but often implies a more general route or path.

there is.ima: Commonly used to express 'there is' or 'there are'.
there is.postoji: A more formal or literal word for 'exists' or 'there is'.

to you.vam: Dative plural or formal singular, meaning 'to you'.
to you.tebi: The informal singular dative form of 'you', meaning 'to you'.

you know.znaš: Informal singular present tense of 'you know'.
you know.znate: Formal or plural version of 'you know'.
you know.poznaješ: Informal singular for 'you are familiar with' or 'you know personally'.
you know.poznajete: Formal or plural version of 'poznaješ', meaning 'you are familiar with'.

said.rekao: Masculine singular past participle of 'to say'. Normally used with an auxiliary.
said.rekli: Masculine or mixed-gender plural past participle of reći; normally used with an auxiliary.
said.rečeno: Passive passive participle meaning 'it was said'.
said.reklo: Neuter singular past participle of reći; normally used with an auxiliary. Passive said is rečeno.

now.sada: Indeclinable adverb; does not change for gender, number or case.

my.mog: Genitive or accusative masculine form of 'moj', used when 'my' is the object or after certain prepositions.
my.mome: Dative/locative masculine of 'moj', meaning 'to my' or 'in my'.

then.onda: The most common word for 'then', meaning 'at that time' or 'next'.
then.tada: Formal or slightly more specific word meaning 'at that moment'.
then.zatim: Often means 'after that' or 'and then' in sequences.
then.tad: Standard short form of tada (then/at that time).
then.potom: A more literary or formal word for 'thereafter' or 'then'.

I would.bih: First-person singular conditional, used to express 'I would'.

who.koja: Feminine form of 'koji', meaning 'which' or 'who' when referring to a feminine noun.
who.kog: Genitive/accusative form of 'tko' or 'koji', meaning 'whom' or 'of whom'.

to him; to it.mu: Short dative pronoun: to him/to it. The full, stressed form is njemu.
to him; to it.njemu: Stressed dative/locative masculine or neuter singular pronoun; short dative form mu.

we will.ćemo: First-person plural future auxiliary ('we will'), used with an infinitive.
we will.hoćemo: Full form meaning 'we will' or 'we want'.

to.do: Preposition meaning 'to' in the sense of reaching a destination.
to.ka: Used to indicate direction 'towards' something, more formal or poetic than 'prema'.

nothing.ničeg: Short genitive form of ništa (nothing); ničega is the longer standard form.

right?.zar: A question particle used to express surprise or seek confirmation, like 'really?' or 'isn't it?'.

us.nas: Genitive/accusative of mi ('we'). The possessive 'our' is naš, not nas.
us.nama: Dative/locative/instrumental of mi (we): to/about/with us. Short dative: nam.

I want.želim: The standard first-person singular for 'I want'.

please.molim: The standard and most common way to say 'please' or 'you're welcome'.
please.molimo: First-person plural present of moliti (ask/beg), commonly a polite please; the same spelling can also be an imperative.
please.moli: Informal imperative singular of 'moliti', meaning 'ask!' or 'please!'.
please.molio: Masculine singular past participle of 'moliti', meaning 'asked' or 'begged'. Normally used with an auxiliary.

say.reći: The infinitive form meaning 'to say' or 'to tell'.
say.reci: Imperative singular, meaning 'say!' or 'tell!' to one person.
say.recite: Formal or plural imperative, meaning 'say!' or 'tell!'.
say.kaži: Singular imperative of kazati (say/tell). A valid standard Croatian form; reci is another common choice.

before; earlier; ago.prije: Can mean 'before' (with genitive), 'earlier', or 'ago' in a time expression.

hey.hej: Interjection for greeting someone or attracting attention; informal.
hey.ej: A softer or more casual version of 'hej', often used to get someone's attention.
hey.haj: Less common, sometimes poetic or used regionally like 'come on'.

I have.imam: First-person singular present of imati. Also the spelling of the noun imam, an Islamic religious leader.

you can.možeš: The informal singular form meaning 'you can'.
you can.možete: Formal or plural version of 'you can'.
you can.smijete: Second-person plural present (also polite singular) of 'smjeti', meaning 'you are allowed to'.

now; USA.sad: Adverb meaning now. Uppercase SAD is also the abbreviation for the United States; matching here ignores case.

you will.ćeš: Second-person singular future auxiliary ('you will'), used with an infinitive.
you will.hoćeš: Full form of 'you will', used for emphasis or in questions.
you will.ćete: Second-person plural short future auxiliary of htjeti; also polite singular. Can precede or follow the infinitive.

because of.zbog: A preposition used to indicate the cause or reason for something.

nor.ni: A conjunction used to introduce a further negative statement.

to us.nam: Short dative of mi ('we'). The stressed form is nama.

there.tamo: The standard word for 'there' in terms of location.
there.ondje: Adverb for there, a location away from the speaker. Onamo indicates movement towards there.
there.eto: Used to point something out that's nearby or just happened, like 'there it is!'.
there.eno: Used to point at something farther away, like 'there they are!'.

people.narod: A more collective or national word for 'the people' or 'a people'.
people.narode: Vocative form of 'narod', used when addressing a people.
people.naroda: Genitive singular; genitive plural of narod (masculine noun).

you are not.nisi: Negative second-person singular of biti. With a past participle it forms a negative past tense.
you are not.niste: Negative second-person plural of biti, also polite singular. A following past participle makes it a negative past tense.

I have to.moram: The present tense form meaning 'I have to' or 'I must'.

always.uvijek: Indeclinable adverb; does not change for gender, number or case.

should.treba: Means 'it is necessary' or 'one should'. It can also mean 'need'.

really.stvarno: A common and neutral way to say 'really' or 'truly'.
really.zaista: A slightly more formal synonym for 'really'.
really.zbilja: Conversational and somewhat emotional version of 'really'.
really.doista: Formal or literary alternative for 'indeed' or 'truly'.
really.itekako: Emphatic form meaning 'very much so' or 'definitely'.

come on.hajde: The standard form for 'come on' or 'let's go'.

per.po: A preposition with multiple meanings, including 'per', 'by', or 'along'.

one.jedan: The masculine form of the number 'one'.
one.jedna: The feminine form of the number 'one'.
one.jednog: Genitive or accusative masculine form of 'jedan', meaning 'one'.
one.jedne: Genitive feminine form or plural feminine nominative of 'jedan', meaning 'of one' or 'one'.
one.jedni: Masculine plural form meaning 'some' or 'certain ones' in contrast.
one.jednim: Instrumental masculine or neuter form of 'jedan', meaning 'with one'.
one.jednoj: Dative/locative feminine of 'jedan', meaning 'to one' or 'in one'.

how much.koliko: Used to ask about quantity, meaning 'how much' or 'how many'.

let's go.idemo: The most common phrase for 'let's go'.
let's go.hajdemo: More formal or older version of 'idemo', still correct and used.
let's go.odemo: First-person plural present of otići (leave/go away). A perfective present; time reference depends on the clause.
let's go.krenemo: First-person plural of 'krenuti', meaning 'let's start' or 'let's set off'.
let's go.krenimo: Imperative form meaning 'let's begin' or 'let's go' with a sense of initiating movement.
let's go.pustimo: First-person plural imperative of 'pustiti', meaning 'let's release' or 'let's go'.
let's go.pođimo: A more literary/formal way to say 'let's go' or 'let us depart'.

you think.misliš: The informal singular present tense of 'you think'.
you think.mislite: Formal or plural form of 'you think'.
you think.razmišljaš: Second-person singular present of 'razmišljati', meaning 'you are thinking' in a more reflective way.
you think.razmisliš: Perfective form meaning 'you think it over' or 'you reflect'.
you think.pomisliš: Used for a sudden or brief thought.

therefore; that is why.zato: Points to a consequence or reason already mentioned. Zato što, as a phrase, means 'because'.

really; exactly.baš: An emphatic particle meaning 'really', 'exactly' or 'just', depending on what it modifies.

than.nego: Used for comparison, similar to 'than' in English.
than.negoli: Conjunction meaning than, especially after a comparative. Negoli is a longer form of nego.

won't.neće: The standard future negative form, meaning 'will not'.

without.bez: Preposition followed by genitive. The colour 'beige' is bež, a different word.

time.vremena: Genitive singular; nominative/genitive/accusative/vocative plural of vrijeme (neuter noun).
time.vremenski: An adjective meaning 'temporal' or 'related to time'.

mine.moja: The feminine singular form of 'my' or 'mine'.
mine.moje: Form of moj ('my'): agrees with the possessed noun. Commonly neuter singular, feminine plural or feminine genitive singular.
mine.moju: Accusative feminine singular of 'moj', meaning 'my' or 'mine'.
mine.mom: Dative/locative masculine of 'moj', meaning 'to my' or 'on my'.
mine.mojoj: Dative/locative feminine of 'moj', meaning 'to my' or 'on my'.
mine.mojim: Dative/instrumental plural of 'moj', meaning 'to my' or 'with my'.
mine.mojih: Genitive plural of 'moj', meaning 'of my' or 'mine'.
mine.mojom: Instrumental feminine of 'moj', meaning 'with my' or 'by my'.
mine.mojem: Alternative dative/locative of 'moj', meaning 'to my' or 'in my'.
mine.mojeg: Genitive masculine/neuter singular of moj; also accusative masculine singular with animate nouns. Not dative.
mine.rudnik: Means 'mine' in the sense of a mining site — not possessive.

we can.možemo: The standard word for 'we can' or 'we are able to'.
we can.smijemo: First-person plural of 'smjeti', meaning 'we are allowed to' or 'we may'.

which.koje: Form of koji: commonly neuter singular or feminine plural; also feminine genitive singular and masculine accusative plural.
which.kojoj: Dative/locative feminine of 'koji', meaning 'to which' or 'in which'.
which.kojem: Dative/locative masculine/neuter of 'koji', meaning 'to which' or 'in which'.
which.kojima: Dative/instrumental plural of 'koji', meaning 'to which' or 'with which'.
which.kojim: Dative/instrumental masculine/neuter plural of 'koji', meaning 'with which' or 'to which'.

it.ono: Neuter singular demonstrative that (over there); also the neuter subject pronoun it.

to her.joj: Short dative of ona ('she'); also an interjection expressing pain, alarm or surprise.
to her.njoj: Stressed dative/locative of ona. The short dative form is joj.

they.oni: The masculine or mixed-gender plural for 'they'.

you want.želite: The formal or plural form of 'you want'.

of that.toga: Genitive singular of taj/to; also masculine animate accusative. Can separately be the noun toga, a Roman garment.

sorry.žao: Used in žao mi je ('I am sorry/I regret it'). The English word 'evil' is not an appropriate hint here.
sorry.oprosti: Informal imperative singular of 'oprostiti', meaning 'forgive me' or 'excuse me'.
sorry.oprostite: The formal or plural imperative of 'oprostiti', meaning 'forgive me' or 'excuse me'.
sorry.izvini: Informal imperative singular of 'izvinuti', meaning 'apologize!' or 'excuse me!'.
sorry.izvinite: Formal or plural imperative of 'izvinuti', meaning 'apologize!' or 'excuse me!'.
sorry.oprostio: Masculine singular past participle of 'oprostiti', meaning 'forgave'. Normally used with an auxiliary.

you have.imaš: The informal singular form of 'you have'.
you have.imate: The formal or plural form of 'you have'.

that.taj: A demonstrative for 'that' when pointing to something nearby and masculine.
that.tog: The genitive form of 'taj', used for possession or after prepositions.
that.onaj: Used for something more distant or specific, meaning 'that one over there'.
that.onoga: The genitive of 'onaj', used when the object is being affected.

of course.naravno: The standard and most common way to say 'of course'.
of course.dakako: A slightly more formal or emphatic synonym for 'naravno'.

to that.tome: Dative/locative masculine or neuter singular of taj/to. The ending does not identify the case without context.
to that.tomu: An alternative dative form of 'to', meaning 'to that'.

could.mogao: Masculine singular past participle of moći ('can'). Used in past and conditional constructions with auxiliaries.
could.mogla: Feminine singular past participle of 'moći', meaning 'could'. Normally used with an auxiliary.
could.mogli: Masculine or mixed-gender plural past participle of 'moći', meaning 'could'. Normally used with an auxiliary.
could.mogle: Feminine plural past participle of 'moći', meaning 'could'. Normally used with an auxiliary.

sir.gospodine: Vocative form used when addressing someone directly as 'Sir'.
sir.gospodina: Genitive/accusative singular; genitive plural of gospodin (masculine noun).

means.znači: The standard verb form meaning 'means' or 'it means'.
means.sredstva: Plural of 'sredstvo', meaning 'means' in the sense of resources or tools.

days.dana: Genitive singular or plural of dan ('day'); also a feminine form of the passive participle dan ('given').
days.dani: Nominative plural meaning 'days' as a subject.
days.dane: Accusative plural, used when 'days' are the object.

never.nikad: Standard short form of nikada (never). Usually used with a negated verb.
never.nikada: More formal or emphatic version of 'nikad'.

your.tvoja: Feminine form of 'tvoj', the informal singular 'your'.
your.tvoje: The neuter form of 'tvoj', the informal singular 'your'.
your.vaš: The masculine singular formal or plural form of 'your'.
your.vaše: Neuter or plural form of 'vaš', the formal/plural 'your'.

were.bili: Masculine or mixed-gender plural past participle of biti; normally used with an auxiliary.
were.bile: Feminine plural past participle of 'biti', meaning 'were'. Normally used with an auxiliary.

she said.rekla: Feminine singular past participle of 'to say'. Normally used with an auxiliary.

time; way; road.put: Means an occasion ('prvi put'), way/journey/road, or 'towards' as a preposition. Context distinguishes these uses.

works.radi: Third person singular of 'raditi' meaning 'he/she/it works'.
works.djela: Plural of 'djelo', meaning 'works' in the sense of creations, deeds, or acts.

year.godine: The plural or genitive form of 'godina', meaning 'years' or 'of the year'.

one's own.svoje: Inflected form of svoj: neuter singular or feminine/masculine plural forms. Refers to the subject’s own possession.
one's own.svoj: Reflexive possessive: one’s own, referring to the subject. Masculine singular; agrees with the possessed noun, not the owner.
one's own.svoju: Accusative feminine singular of svoj (one’s own), agreeing with the possessed noun; refers back to the subject.
one's own.svojim: Instrumental masculine/neuter singular or dative/locative/instrumental plural of svoj; the owner is the subject.
one's own.svog: Short genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of svoj (one’s own).
one's own.svom: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular or instrumental feminine singular of svoj; possession refers to the subject.
one's own.svojoj: Dative/locative feminine singular of svoj (one’s own), agreeing with the possessed noun.
one's own.svojih: Genitive plural of svoj, all genders. Means one’s own, with the owner determined by the subject.
one's own.svojom: Instrumental feminine singular of svoj (one’s own); the subject determines whose possession it is.
one's own.svoja: Feminine singular or neuter plural of svoj (one’s own), agreeing with the possessed noun.
one's own.svoga: Long genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of svoj (one’s own).
one's own.svome: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular of svoj (one’s own); the possessor is the subject.
one's own.svojem: Dative/locative masculine/neuter singular of svoj (one’s own), an alternative to svom/svome.
one's own.svojeg: Genitive masculine/neuter singular, or animate masculine accusative singular, of svoj (one’s own).

you have to.moraš: Informal singular form meaning 'you have to' or 'you must'.
you have to.morate: Formal or plural version of 'you have to'.

give; come on.daj: Singular imperative of dati ('give'); also used conversationally to urge someone: 'come on'.

don't.nemoj: Imperative singular form meaning 'don’t', used to tell one person not to do something.
don't.nemojte: Formal or plural imperative, used when addressing more than one person or politely.

god.bože: Vocative form used when calling out to God.
god.bog: Nominative form, the standard word for 'God' or 'god'.

I won't.neću: Standard future negative of 'I will not'.

someone.nekoga: Genitive/accusative form of 'netko', meaning 'someone' as the object.
someone.nekog: Shortened or informal genitive/accusative of 'netko', used in speech.
someone.nekoj: Dative feminine of 'neki', meaning 'to some' or 'to someone'.

to me.meni: Dative/locative of ja; a stressed form, often used after prepositions. Separately, meni can mean a restaurant menu.

at; near; code.kod: Preposition with genitive for location 'at/by/near'; also a masculine noun meaning 'code'.

thought.mislio: Masculine singular past participle of 'to think'. Normally used with an auxiliary.
thought.mislila: Feminine singular past participle of 'misliti', meaning 'thought'. Normally used with an auxiliary.
thought.mislili: Plural past participle of 'misliti', meaning 'thought'. Normally used with an auxiliary.
thought.pomislio: Masculine form of 'had a sudden thought'.
thought.pomislili: Plural of 'pomislio', used when a group suddenly thought of something.

see.vidjet: Infinitive of vidjeti; the dictionary form does not specify person or tense.

looks like.izgleda: The most common way to say 'looks like'.
looks like.sliči: Present third-person singular of sličiti (resemble), used with dative: sliči majci. Ličiti means paint/whitewash.
